content.body:
`ascribe-lsp`'s `openapi::openapi_a_renamed_operation_is_fixed_from_the_review_s_base` failed once on ubuntu CI ([#1093's run](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/40371865538)) and passed on re-run. It failed at `assert!(safe, "the rename is safe")` (`crates/ascribe-lsp/tests/all/openapi.rs:325`), after `titles[0]` had already matched `` Link to `../api/openapi.yaml#fetchUser` ``. So the fix was the right one, but it was still the unsafe guess made without the base.

## Why

`set_base_request` (`crates/ascribe-lsp/src/server.rs`, around line 1212) calls `core.remember_base_apis(...)`. That applies `Change::BaseApis` and queues the affected files as dirty. The function then calls `shared.wake.notify_all()`, but it never stores `shared.idle = false`. Notifications do set it: `if core.busy() { shared.idle.store(false, …) }` at the end of notification handling, around line 425.

Until the diagnostics worker wakes and plans the job, `idle` therefore still reads `true` from the round before. The test's `client.settle()` (`tests/support/mod.rs:237`) can see that stale `true` and return straight away. `diagnostic()` then returns the `link-operation-missing` published before the base was set, whose fixes were computed without the base's operation ids. Whether this happens depends on whether the worker thread wins the race to the lock, which explains why the failure is rare.

This is a reading of the code that I haven't reproduced. Other requests that apply changes (for example `edit_request` and `project_edit_request`) may have the same gap, and are worth checking at the same time.

## Done when

- Every request handler that queues work leaves `idle` false before it answers, as notification handling does. A shared helper for this would be better than a line per handler.
- `settle()` after `ascribe/review/setBase` only returns once the round that uses the base has been published.
- The test passes reliably when run in a loop (for example 200 runs, or under `--test-threads` contention), and stays unchanged apart from the fix.

Phase 1 of 5 of [Load a project once](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/workspace/README.md), the plan for #994 ([decision #994](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/decisions/994-one-workspace.md)). ## What to do

Each command reads each source file once per run and indexes the project once. Loading keeps the `Sources` listing it read, and `Held` gives it back, so `Project::index` becomes the one shared index (`link_index`) instead of reading every source a second time.

This is the first phase, and it needs nothing before it. Phase 2 needs it. The phases run one at a time and in order.

- A test counts reads through a counting `FileSystem`: each command's library entry over `examples/quill` reads each source once and lists once. It fails on `main`.
- `node scripts/compare/outputs.ts --base main` shows nothing (label `optimization`).
- The perf benchmark (`cargo bench -p ascribe-corpora --bench perf`) is no slower on the synthetic project and the Elastic sample.
- ARCHITECTURE.md's "Loading a project, and reading files" no longer says the commands index twice.

The keystroke bench fails its own criterion on `main`: a file that no page reads must cost less than a tenth of a page written on disk, but it now costs 250 ms (`a file no page reads cost 250.186032ms, a page written on disk 29.384014ms`, at `crates/ascribe-lsp/benches/keystroke.rs:432`). The weekly Corpora run is red too.

`Core::did_change_watched` calls `addresses.changed()` for every event, so any file written on disk, a build's output included, queues a comparison of the addresses and keeps the server busy for `addresses::SETTLE` (250 ms) before it goes idle. Found in https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/1112#issuecomment-6425848966.

**Done looks like:** the addresses are marked changed only for events that can change them (a source page, a side file such as `ascribe.addresses`, the model or a `[from]` file, an API spec, git's refs). A file no page reads leaves them alone, and the keystroke bench passes. The busy marking from #1096 / #1098 stays as it is.

Touches: `crates/ascribe-lsp/src/core.rs`, `crates/ascribe-lsp/src/addresses.rs`.

Found by the fuzz targets added for #1020.

## What's wrong

A lone `` (not followed by `
`) in some places makes the spans after it point one byte early. The parser treats a lone `` as a line ending elsewhere (`tree.rs`'s line splitting, `nest.rs`), so this looks like one place that counts it differently.

**In frontmatter**, the formatter then edits the wrong bytes, and formatting isn't idempotent:

```text
"---
"
---

@note:{"
 -> "---
"
---

@note :{"     (the space goes before the colon, not after it)
 -> "---
"
---

@not  :{"     (and the second pass eats the `e`)
```

The directive's span is `11..18`; its text is at `12..19`. With `
` instead of the lone `` (`"---

---

x"`), the spans are right.

**In a link reference definition**, `"[r]:[]"` gives a text inline whose value is `"]"` and whose span covers `"["` (`check_tree` in `crates/ascribe-syntax/tests/support/mod.rs` reports it).

## Done when

- Both inputs parse with every span covering its own text (`check_tree` reports nothing), and `"---
"
---

@note:{"` formats once to its canonical form.
- `cargo fuzz run format` (from `fuzz/`, CONTRIBUTING.md) runs without finding this again.

content.body:
Found by the fuzz targets added for #1020.

## What's wrong

`check_tree` (`crates/ascribe-syntax/tests/support/mod.rs`), the span checker the parser's tests use, holds every container's span to end where its end line or last block does, without trailing whitespace. An unclosed container at the end of a file doesn't:

```text
"@memo:\n"
  block     0..7 "@memo:\n": ends with a line ending
  container 0..7 "@memo:\n": ends with whitespace
  container 0..7 "@memo:\n": doesn't end where its end line or last block does
```

and with content, `"…@memo:\n  - Not an item.\n\n   "` gives a container span ending in the blank lines after its last block.

Either the span is wrong, or `check_tree`'s rule should say what an unclosed container's span is. Whichever is decided, the parser and the checker should agree.

## Done when

- `check_tree` reports nothing for an unclosed container, and the decision is in a test.
- The `parse` fuzz target (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse.rs`) can then hold all of `check_tree`, not only the in-bounds check, once the lone carriage return issue is fixed too.

content.body:
Found by the differential test's new generator (#988).

## What's wrong

A fresh load (`Project::assemble`) reads every file's snippets through one `CodeFiles`, so each code file gets the next id from `CODE_FILE_IDS` in the order the project first reads it. `IncrementalProject::apply` resolves each file's snippets with a new `CodeFiles` (`crates/ascribe-resolve/src/incremental/mod.rs`, the `resolve_snippets` calls), so the first code file each file reads is `0x8000_0000`. After an update, two different code files can share an id, and a code file's id differs from the one a fresh load gives it.

`Snippet::file` is read as a code file's identity: `reading::find` keys its line indexes by `block.file`, and the language server's search (`crates/ascribe-lsp/src/search.rs`, `code_text`) finds a code file's text by it. So in the editor, a search match in the second code file can get the first one's line numbers or text.

Smallest case: start from disk with `docs/_shared.md` showing `code:app.py#main`, then edit `docs/index.md` to `@snippet: code:lib.py`. The incremental snapshot gives `lib.py` id `0x8000_0000`, the same as `app.py`; a fresh load gives it `0x8000_0001`.

## Done when

- A code file's id after any sequence of updates is what a fresh load with the same ids gives it, or ids are by path in both, so two code files never share one.
- `code_ids_hidden` in `crates/ascribe-resolve/tests/incremental_support/mod.rs` is gone, and the differential test compares the ids.

content.body:
The rest of #965. #1133 writes the conventions down in CONTRIBUTING.md ("Command-line conventions", decision #965) and adds `crates/ascribe-cli/src/conventions.rs`, which holds them over the `clap` definitions with an `EXCEPTIONS` list of today's breaks. This issue is the commands themselves: each pull request takes a group of commands, brings them in line, and removes their entries from `EXCEPTIONS`. The test fails on an entry that's no longer needed, so the list can only shrink.

Today's exceptions, by rule:

- **`--dry-run` and `--force` (the git guard):** `init`, `check` (`--fix`), `fmt`, `rename`, `baseline write`, `baseline prune`, `permalinks sync`, `permalinks retire`, `addresses init`, `addresses move`, `addresses retire`, `sources fetch`, `sources update`, `observe`, `templates eject`, `vale eject`, `agents sync`, `agents index`.
- **`--exit-code`:** `check`, whose `--deny-warnings` becomes an alias of `--exit-code=warning`.
- **`--format json`:** `sources fetch`, `templates list`, `vale eject`, `agents sync`, `agents prompt`.
- **`concise` beside `text`:** every command with `--format` apart from `check` (35 commands): an alias of `text` where a command has no one-line form.

The test can't read two of the conventions from `clap`, so they need output tests in the pull requests that change these commands:

- `--check` prints each change as a unified diff (`fmt`, `permalinks sync`, `agents sync`, `observe`).
- A revision given where a path goes is answered with `--base`. `drift` does this already; `diff` doesn't yet.

A renamed option keeps its old spelling as a hidden alias for a release. `observe --check` keeps working in CI throughout, and #979 changes `observe` too, so whichever lands second follows the other.

## Done looks like

- `EXCEPTIONS` in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/conventions.rs` is empty.
- `fmt --check` prints a unified diff, and `diff HEAD` says `--base HEAD`, each with a test.

Found by the `parse` fuzz target while working on #1139. It's on main too and doesn't involve `\r`.

## What's wrong

When a table's header line is indented and its delimiter row has an alignment colon, a body cell's span stops one byte short of the text inside it:

```text
" s\n:-\nc\n"
  inline Span { start: 7, end: 8 } "\n": outside its parent Span { start: 7, end: 7 }
```

content.body:
**The problem you're trying to solve:**

`cargo deny --locked check advisories` (rust.yml's dependencies job, and `pnpm check:all`) now fails with [RUSTSEC-2024-0449](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0449): `unsafe-libyaml` 0.2.11 is unmaintained. Its repository was archived in March 2024, and it's a c2rust translation of libyaml, so bugs found in it won't be fixed upstream. The advisory says no safe upgrade is available. The step doesn't fail CI, since a new advisory can appear with no change here (CONTRIBUTING.md asks for this issue).

It comes in through `serde_yaml_ng` 0.10 (the workspace dependency in `Cargo.toml`), which `ascribe-check`, `ascribe-cli`, `ascribe-diff`, `ascribe-emit`, `ascribe-lsp`, `ascribe-model`, `ascribe-query`, `ascribe-resolve`, and `ascribe-templates` use, for frontmatter and the OpenAPI specs among other things.

The advisory suggests YAML parsers in safe Rust: [saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/saphyr) (with [serde-saphyr](https://crates.io/crates/serde-saphyr) for serde) or [noyalib](https://crates.io/crates/noyalib).

**Done when:** one of these holds, with the choice recorded:

- `serde_yaml_ng` is replaced by a YAML parser in safe Rust, with every output, diagnostic, and JSON byte for byte the same (`node scripts/compare/outputs.ts --base main`), or with any difference named and accepted by a decision; or
- RUSTSEC-2024-0449 is ignored in `.cargo/deny.toml` with this issue as the reason, if the risk is accepted for now.

Found by `pnpm check:all` while working on #977 (#1156), which doesn't touch dependencies.

content.body:
Found by the `parse` fuzz target while working on #1149 (PR #1158). It fails on main too and doesn't involve tables.

## What's wrong

When a paragraph's continuation line is indented and a code span on it runs onto the next line, the text after the code span gets a span that overlaps the code span's:

```text
"x\n `\n`c"
  inline Span { start: 6, end: 7 } "c": overlaps the inline before it
"\x0b\n `\na`c"
  inline Span { start: 7, end: 8 } "c": overlaps the inline before it
```

The fuzzer's original inputs were `"\0\r `\n`D"` and `"\x0b\n `\n`c"`; `cargo fuzz tmin` and some hand reduction brought them down to the first line above. Without the indent (`"x\n`\n`c"`) or without the line break inside the code span (`"\x0b\n `a`c"`), the spans are right. So the code span's end is likely computed without the continuation line's stripped indent (the paragraph's `line_offsets`) once it crosses a line, and comes out one byte late per indent space.

## Done when

- The text after such a code span has the span of its own text, and these inputs are in `directives_in_every_container` (`crates/ascribe-syntax/tests/all/spans.rs`).
- The `parse` fuzz target runs clean on them.

**The problem you're trying to solve:**

#1005's decision builds on `draft: true`: a template's leftover placeholder is an error on a page that publishes and advice on a draft, and `ascribe new` writes `draft: true`. The issue says main has it, but it doesn't: nothing in SPEC.md, the content model, `check`, or `build` reads a `draft` key, and a page with `draft: true` today is an undeclared frontmatter field. Kyle chose to add it as its own change first, then finish #1005 on top of it (26 October 2026, in the #1005 thread).

- `draft: true` in a page's frontmatter is a reserved key, like `type` and `intended`, defined in SPEC.md with the decision recorded in `project-docs/decisions/`, since SPEC.md is a contract.

- A link from a published page to a draft page is reported, since the reader would get nothing there (which diagnostic and level is the implementor's call, following the existing pattern for content a build leaves out).

content.body:
On `main` (f9180e9), releasing the docs' planned line fails at step 2 of RELEASING.md:

```sh
ascribe versions release "ascribe 0.4.5" --next 0.4.6 --config docs --dry-run
```

```
Error: archiving the line that was current would change what a reader sees, in site/plain/agents.md, site/plain/agents/claude-code.md, … (every page of site/plain, and site/plain/llms.txt); nothing was written
```

The change it finds is the agents' preamble at the top of each plain page, which names the live lines. With 0.4.4 and 0.4.5 both live (after the release's move step), it says:

```
> … This documentation describes Ascribe 0.4.5 and 0.4.4. Anything marked in main, not yet released isn't in any of those releases yet.
```

and with 0.4.4 archived:

```
> … This documentation describes Ascribe 0.4.5. Anything marked in main, not yet released isn't in that release yet.
```

That's the change archiving the line is supposed to make. But step 6 of `release` in `crates/ascribe-lsp/src/release.rs` compares the outputs before and after the archive (`compare(&after_move, &archived)`) and treats any difference as unexpected. The sentence is written in `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/llms.rs` (around line 428). It probably arrived with #1028 (PR #1160), which added the release sentence after the last release.

## Done when

- `ascribe versions release "ascribe <planned>" --next <next> --config docs` works on `main`, and it still refuses an archive that changes anything else a reader sees.
- A test in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/` releases a project whose build writes the agents' preamble with more than one live line, so this doesn't come back.

Found while doing #973 (PR #1174).

content.body:
Two gaps in what `ascribe agents sync` writes for a project in a subfolder, found running it on our own `docs/` in #1171 (for #1008).

## The page types get cut first

`docs/AGENTS.md` lists none of the docs' six page types. All it says is "…and 6 more: `cargo run -q -p ascribe-cli -- model docs --section types`". The 4,000-character budget cuts the types before anything else, and a long `--command` uses more of the budget. Types are what an agent needs most before it writes a page, since every page names one with `type:`.

## The skill's commands assume the project is where the agent runs

Step 4 of the skill's loop, `… check` with no file, and `… model` with no `--config` both exit 2 from this repository's root, which has no `ascribe.toml`. `docs/AGENTS.md` gets this right with `--config docs`. Sync could pass the `--config` it was given into the skill's commands too, as it already does for `AGENTS.md`. This only works when every project in the repository shares the skill, so it needs the same care that `--command` gets in `commands_of`.

## Done looks like

- The page types are cut last, after the sentences that are cut now, or a type's line gets shorter, so that `docs/AGENTS.md` lists all six types.
- In a repository whose only project is in a subfolder, the skill's commands work from the root.
- `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/agents.rs` covers both, and the docs' files are synced again.

Say a `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md` with its own `@AGENTS.md` line, outside Ascribe's markers, as this repository's root did before #1171. `ascribe agents sync --target claude` then appends its marked block, which holds another `@AGENTS.md`, so the file imports it twice. #1171 worked around this by replacing the hand-written line with the block.

`claude_md` and the `add` call in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/agents/sync.rs` place the block whatever the file already says. The `CLAUDE.local.md` branch already checks `contains("@AGENTS.md")`.

## Done looks like

- When a `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md` outside the markers, sync writes no block there. It leaves the file as it is and says the file already loads `AGENTS.md`. `--check` counts that file as up to date.
- A test in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/agents.rs` covers this, beside the test that already checks a `CLAUDE.md` with text of its own.

content.body:
Found reviewing #1185, which has the skill tell agents to run `ascribe addresses move --config <folder> <old> <page>` and `addresses retire --config <folder> <old>` from the repository's root.

`ascribe addresses move --help` says `OLD` and `NEW` are "a page's path, from the current folder or from the content root". With `--config`, a path from the current folder isn't accepted. In a repository with `examples/quill` copied to `docs/` (so its content root is `docs/docs/`), run from the repository's root:

- `ascribe addresses move --config docs docs/docs/webhooks.md docs/docs/hooks.md` exits 2: "`docs/docs/hooks.md` isn't a page of the project". `… webhooks.md hooks.md` works.
- `ascribe addresses retire --config docs docs/docs/quickstart.md --reason x` exits 0 and records `docs/docs/quickstart.md` as retired. That's no page's address, so `quickstart.md` is still lost and nothing says so at the time.

## Done looks like

- With `--config`, a page's path from the current folder works for `addresses move` and `addresses retire`, as the help says. Otherwise the help says what's true, and `retire` refuses an old path that resolves outside the content root.
- A test in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/` runs both from a folder above the project with `--config`.
content.title: `addresses move`/`retire` with `--config` read a page's path from the content root, not the current folder

content.body:
This is the rest of #1134, as #1134 was the rest of #965. PR #1187 brought the `--format json` group into line, so `Rule::Json` has no exceptions left. This issue covers the groups still listed in `EXCEPTIONS` in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/conventions.rs`. Each pull request takes one group, brings its commands into line with CONTRIBUTING.md's "Command-line conventions" (decision #965), and removes their entries. The test fails on an entry that's no longer needed, so the list can only shrink.

The exceptions left, by rule:

- **`--dry-run` and `--force` (the git guard):** `init`, `check` (`--fix`), `fmt`, `rename`, `baseline write`, `baseline prune`, `permalinks sync`, `permalinks retire`, `addresses init`, `addresses move`, `addresses retire`, `sources fetch`, `sources update`, `observe`, `templates eject`, `vale eject`, `agents sync`, `agents index`.
- **`--exit-code`:** `check`. Its `--deny-warnings` becomes an alias of `--exit-code=warning`. This waits for #1022 (PR #1135), which changes `check`'s output options.
- **`concise` beside `text`:** every command with `--format` apart from `check`, `sources fetch`, `templates list`, `vale eject`, `agents sync`, and `agents prompt`: 35 commands. `concise` is an alias of `text` where a command has no one-line form. `answer::TextFormat` (added in #1187) already has the alias, and most of these commands use `answer::Format` or an enum of their own.

The test can't read two of the conventions from `clap`, so the pull requests that change these commands need output tests for them:

- `--check` prints each change as a unified diff (`fmt`, `permalinks sync`, `agents sync`, `observe`).
- A revision given where a path goes is answered with `--base`. `drift` does this already. `diff` doesn't yet.

A renamed option keeps its old spelling as a hidden alias for a release. `observe --check` keeps working in CI throughout. #979 also changes `observe`, so whichever of the two lands second follows the other.

## Done looks like

- `EXCEPTIONS` in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/conventions.rs` is empty.
- `fmt --check` prints a unified diff, and `diff HEAD` says `--base HEAD`, each with a test.

content.body:
Found reviewing #931.

**What happens.** A base build is matched, by the rename heuristic in `matched` (`crates/ascribe-check/src/addresses/mod.rs`), to an older line whose base is under the line's folder, and in the same change `[consumer] agents` goes from on to off. For each Markdown address, `moved_by` returns `[Agents, BasePath]`. `compare` filters that against `changes()`, which has no base-path change because `base-path` didn't move, so the result is `[AgentsOff]`. Once `[former] agents = [true]` is recorded, that counts as recorded and the address is skipped.

But `former_pairs` (`crates/ascribe-emit/src/site/redirects.rs`) forwards Markdown versions only from today's base (`router.markdown_url`), not from the old base without the line's folder. So the old `.md` addresses are neither forwarded in `redirects.json` nor reported as `address-lost`.

**What done looks like.** Either those addresses are forwarded, or the check reports them like any other lost page (as #931 now does for the page addresses in the same situation). A test in `crates/ascribe-check/tests/all/addresses_settings.rs` covers it, with a conformance case under `tests/conformance/cases/addresses/`.

content.body:
The assets contract (docs/content/contracts/assets.md, §2 step 5) lets a page reference any file inside the project root, so a link such as `[config](../.git/config)` is an asset: a build copies the checkout's `.git/config` to `_ascribe/up/.git/config`, the HTML report inlines it, and an archive carries it. On a CI runner, with `actions/checkout`'s default `persist-credentials`, that file holds the job's token.

Decision, from the security review's phase 6 (the maintainer, 29 October 2026): a file under a `.git` folder is never an asset. The reference is reported as `link-target-missing` or `image-source-missing`, with a message of its own, and nothing copies it. The contract's step 5 says so; this issue numbers the decision file.
